question: How does PL/M-80 V4.0 return a parameterless BYTE constant to a caller that stores it in a static BYTE?

toolchain.simulator: z80pack Intel Intellec MDS-800 Simulator Release 1.39
toolchain.manual: Intel PL/M-80 Programming Manual, order 9800268B, January 1980, sections 8.1.3 and 8.2
toolchain.overlay_provenance_note: The local recipe labels PLM80 and OV0-OV4 V4.0 and OV5-OV6 V3.1. Individual overlay opens were not traced; the banner reports V4.0 but per-run overlay provenance/use remains unresolved.

input.syntax_basis: Intel PL/M-80 Programming Manual: typed procedure type follows PROCEDURE; typed procedure uses RETURN expression; typed procedure call is used as a function reference in an expression.
input.input_terminator: One Ctrl-Z was sent to COPY :CI: as console EOF; it is not part of the 97-byte stored source file.

commands: connect /usr/bin/telnet 127.0.0.1 4010; send exactly one ASCII SPACE byte (20H)
COPY each BYTRTN artifact TO :HP:; capture via /tmp/.z80pack/intelmdssim.pt
direct_observations: The listing identifies P as a typed BYTE procedure at code offset 000BH with size 3 and reports PROCEDURE STACK=0000H.
The listing gives RESULT offset 0000H, size 1; the module VARIABLE area is 0001H and LOCATE maps DATA to 369CH.
At 368BH P executes MVI A,2AH followed by RET at 368DH; there is no other callee epilogue instruction.
MAIN calls P at 368BH from 3683H. Its next instruction, at 3686H, is STA 369CH, storing A directly into RESULT.
MAIN initializes SP to 369CH. CALL's return address is 3686H; P enters with SP=369AH and direct RET restores SP=369CH. Maximum stack use is 2 bytes.
The LINK map includes only BYTRTN.OBJ(MAIN); PLM80.LIB was not needed.
The compiler accepted the exact source form with zero program errors.
sample_specific_interpretation: In this no-parameter BYTE-return sample, emitted code places the returned constant in A and the immediate caller stores it directly with STA. This does not establish a universal return convention.
unresolved_questions: The local mixed-overlay recipe's individual PLM80 overlay provenance and whether OV5/OV6 were opened remain unverified.
This fixture does not establish return conventions for ADDRESS, multi-byte values, parameterized/external procedures, or other PL/M-80 compiler versions.
